$comment: THE schema for the P14 Step-0 spec-traceability inventory — the single place the verdict vocabulary and the
per-verdict evidence requirements are written down. Three consumers read THIS file rather than carrying their
own copy: scripts/spec/build_inventory.py (which derives each row's GAP/OK state),
scripts/spec/record_verdicts.py (which validates an incoming batch before merging it), and the C# battery gate
SpecTraceabilityInventoryDriftTests (which enforces referential integrity against the working tree).
It is DATA, not code, for the reason CLAUDE.md rule 5 gives: a hand-maintained list in three languages drifts,
and the DA wave's lesson (feedback_one_rule_one_place) was that every symptom traced back to one rule written
down more than once. Adding a verdict here is the whole change.
Definition of DONE per docs/rearchitecture/DESIGN-spec-conformance-review.md section 1: every normative rule has
(a) a located implementation OR a recorded owner documented-non-support decision, (b) a verdict verified against
the spec TEXT, and (c) a spec-derived test. A row is OK only when all three hold; everything else is a GAP, and
the GAP count is the v1.0 burn-down metric (owner decision D13: zero GAP = P14 DONE).
$verdict-vs-state: ⛔ 'requires' IS NOT THE SAME QUESTION AS 'does this row close'. `requires` lists the evidence a RECORD must
carry to be well-formed — the evidence for the VERDICT itself. Closing the row additionally needs a
spec-derived covering test (see test-ref below). Keeping them apart is what makes CONFORMS-but-untested
expressible, and DESIGN-spec-conformance-review.md §3 Phase C names that category outright: 'CONFORMS-but-
untested → write the spec-derived golden (so coverage is DURABLE, not merely asserted)'.
It is a genuinely useful state — the rule is verified, and the row is one golden away from done — and
collapsing it into either CONFORMS-and-closed or PARTIAL would lose that. The first Phase-B batch produced
seven of them on its first run.
The same split is what makes a DOCUMENTED-BUT-UNPINNED Annex A.1 row expressible (see `kinds` below): the
§7 determination is written, filed under its own item and correct, and no test yet pins the behaviour it
describes. 19 of the 37 rows the first A.1 back-fill recorded are exactly that — the identical legitimate Phase-C
category as CONFORMS-but-untested, not a defect in the batch.

CONFORMS.meaning: The implementation was read and agrees with the spec text across every applicable edition. Closes the row only once a SPEC-DERIVED test covers it; until then the row is CONFORMS-but-untested and stays a GAP. On a kind-DOC row the 'implementation' read is the DETERMINATION: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 states what this implementor-defined element does, and the compiler does it. ⚠ A determination that READS negative is still CONFORMS where the not-providing is itself the implementor's answer to A.1's question AND the item is one the standard REQUIRES. ⛔ Where the item is OPTIONAL and the determination opens 'Not provided.', the verdict is DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT — owner decision, kb/Work PB280 Q1, 2026-09-02, applied as the `a1-optional-not-provided` derived selector rather than row by row (items 7, 64, 106, 127, 143, 150, 193 and 196 on 2026-09-24, up to 30 as the register fills; item 206 was one of the first two until owner decision Q30, 2026-09-09 — kb/Work PB592 — found the element IS provided, so its cell now opens 'Provided' and the row carries an adjudicated CONFORMS). The question was open here until then and no agent was permitted to answer it.

DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT.meaning: An OWNER decision (never an agent's) that a language element is not supported, and is DOCUMENTED as unsupported. Three grounds, not one: ISO 4.2.16 (the conformance claim itself), 4.2.7 for an OPTIONAL element ('An implementor shall identify in user documentation the optional language elements for which that implementor claims support'), and 4.2.6 for a PROCESSOR-DEPENDENT one ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation'). The 4.2.16-only wording was too narrow and was widened 2026-08-31: the verdict already carried processor-dependent declines and rules whose stated range no host can satisfy, neither of which is an optional module. The notes field carries the decision reference; closing still needs a test proving we diagnose (or, where the departure is a reported VALUE rather than a rejected construct, that the documented behaviour is what actually happens) rather than silently miscompile. ⛔ ON A KIND-DOC ROW IT HAS TWO GROUNDS, AND THEY DIFFER IN WHETHER §7 CARRIES A ROW — which is why `anchor-exempt-verdicts` is not read on the verdict alone (see `kinds`). (a) The CONDITIONING FACILITY is not implemented, so A.1's provision precondition is unmet and the item is WITHDRAWN — there is no element left to document ('When the element is part of a feature that is optional or processor-dependent, the item is not required if the optional or processor-dependent feature is not implemented' — A.1 preamble); §7 carries NO row (items 84, 85, 173, 86), and items 13 and 15 — forming and locating a non-COBOL program name — are the next of the shape, once the owner records that the §4.2.3 interaction is unclaimed. (b) The item is OPTIONAL and the ELEMENT is not provided (kb/Work PB280 Q1, owner 2026-09-02): A.1's preamble conditions the documentation duty on provision ('Documentation required: If the element is provided by the implementor …'), §4.2.7 obliges us to identify what we claim, and §7 DOES carry the row, because stating the non-provision is the determination. Such a row is anchored, and its witness must prove the documented posture is what actually happens.

DIVERGES.meaning: The implementation contradicts the spec. The notes field carries the CONFORMANCE-FIX-QUEUE item id that owns the fix. On a kind-DOC row: §7 documents one thing and the compiler does another — the failure §7's own preamble calls worse than an undocumented determination, and which had no expressible form until a DOC row could carry a verdict at all.

PARTIAL.meaning: Implemented for some editions, operand shapes or paths but not all. The notes field states which.

NOT-IMPLEMENTED.meaning: No implementation was located. The notes field states what is absent — a staged COBOLNET0899, a loud reject, or nothing at all.

NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION.meaning: An unanswered question, deliberately still a GAP: an unanswered question is not coverage. The notes field carries the bare question.

$comment: A verdict that follows MECHANICALLY from one owner determination plus the rule's own SCOPE, rather than
being adjudicated row by row. The selector is DATA here so the batch generator (Python —
scripts/spec/inventory_schema.py DerivedSelector, driven by scripts/spec/derive_verdict_batch.py) and the
drift test (C# — DerivedVerdictDriftTests.Select) read the SAME predicate; writing it twice is how the
mode-set drift of kb/Work PB194 happened.
⚠ THAT SENTENCE WAS FALSE UNTIL 2026-09-02 AND IS NOW TRUE. From PB198 until the A.4 landing there was no
Python consumer of `derived-verdicts` at all — grep found this file, the C# test and the docs — so the
PB198 batch was produced by hand and the second reader that justifies writing a predicate as data was an
aspiration. Three of the six A.4 refuters found it independently. The evaluator now lives in
inventory_schema.py and both engines call it.
⛔ A derived verdict is NOT a shortcut past adjudication. It applies only where a single decision leaves
nothing to adjudicate PER ROW — and the drift test then holds every selected row at that verdict, which is
what stops the population drifting back into five states. Two shapes qualify, and it took the second one
landing (2026-09-02) to notice that the first had been written down as if it were the definition:
· the decision makes an entire rule UNREACHABLE — the seven A.4 module declines; or
· the decision answers, once, a question every row of a CLASS asks in the same words — kb/Work PB280 Q1
('a §7 determination of "Not provided." on an A.1-OPTIONAL item closes as DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT'),
where the rules are perfectly reachable and it is the ADJUDICATION that is common to all of them.
A selector of the second shape must be read twice as carefully, because its rows are live surface: the
protection is that its arms turn on what the OWNER wrote (the requirement class the standard states, and
the determination this repository filed), never on an agent's reading of a rule's text.
⛔ AND IT IS NOT A SHORTCUT PAST THE WITNESS EITHER. DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT resolves, but a row closes only
on a test proving the documented posture is what ACTUALLY happens (see $verdict-vs-state). Every row these
eight selectors stamp stays a GAP until its witness lands; the verdict is the cheap half.
$arms: THE SHAPE. `arms` is a DISJUNCTION of CONJUNCTIONS: within one arm every field that is present must hold,
a rule is selected when ANY arm holds, and the entry's `excludes-patterns` then drop it whatever arm took
it. Fields, each of which exists because a module needed it and the flat requires-sections/requires-pattern
pair could not say it:
· `sections`       — the rule's OWN clause, matched COMPONENT-WISE (see below). PB198's lesson: §8.8.1.4
is TITLED for the declined mode and its rules never repeat the phrase.
· `pattern`        — the rule's TEXT (always case-insensitive in both engines; a data pattern must not
depend on an option the reader sets — A.4.13's arm turns on the capital F of
'File-name-1' and case-sensitively selects 11 rules instead of 12).
· both together    — an AND-gate. `file-name-1` is STATEMENT-LOCAL: in §13.4.5.4 it is the file
description entry's own subject, so A.4.13's text ungated selects 176 rules, not 12.
The same gate is the only way to reach a rule scoped by OPERAND NAME — §12.3.7.3's
data-name-1/-2 ARE the CURSOR and CRT STATUS operands and nothing else, and the
rules constraining them carry no screen vocabulary and sit in a shared clause.
· `xref-sections`  — a clause citation inside the rule's text, '(13.18.24, FORMAT clause, General rule
10)', which is how an Annex A.1 documentation obligation names the clause that
creates it. Keyed on the SAME clause numbers as the clause arm, so adding a module
clause extends the A.1 arm for free instead of silently not extending it.
· `requirement`    — the A.1 REQUIREMENT CLASS the standard states in the item's own text ('This item is
optional.'), carried on the catalog row: 164 required · 30 optional · 27
conditionally required · 1 unclassified. The A.1 preamble writes its licences PER
CLASS, so a selector deriving from one of them must read the class and not infer it.
· `determination-prefix` — what docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 SAYS about the element, read off the register row
keyed by the rule's own id (which is exactly the anchor `kinds.DOC.anchor-template`
computes), leading markdown emphasis stripped, matched case-insensitively on the
cell's OPENING words. It is the first arm field that reads an artifact outside the
catalog, and it has to be: a DOC row's implementation IS its determination. An item
with no §7 row is never selected — a missing determination is not a negative one.
⚠ Neither of these two axes is falsifiable against today's data (all 30 optional
items and all 47 §7 rows agree), so each is driven against fabricated data by
`python scripts/spec/derive_verdict_batch.py --self-test`, which the C# gate shells.
· `kinds` / `excludes-kinds` — the rule's KIND, per ARM, which is the point. A general format (kind FMT)
is evidence about a CLAUSE, never about one of its formats, so the TEXT axis must
never select one: without `excludes-kinds` on the text arm, FMT-14.9.1.2 and
FMT-14.9.11.2 — the ACCEPT and DISPLAY general formats, both PARTIAL, carrying the
compiler's most-used statements — flip to non-support because their optional format
names screen-name-1. The CLAUSE axis still takes FMT-13.17.2, every format of which
IS screen. A kind field also replaced A.4.3's `^<pre` exclusion, a RENDERING proxy
for a kind predicate that leaks: 56 of 322 FMT rows do not match it.
⛔ SECTION PREFIXES MATCH COMPONENT-WISE, AND THAT IS A CORRECTION, NOT A CONVENIENCE. A clause number is a
dotted PATH. Both engines matched it with a raw string prefix test until 2026-09-02, under which §13.18.30
falls inside §13.18.3 and §13.18.40 (PICTURE) inside §13.18.4 (BACKGROUND-COLOR). Measured on the screen
selector, whose clause arm names five such prefixes: the raw test selects 543 rules where the component-wise
test selects 156 — 387 extra, 33 of them already adjudicated (32 CONFORMS + 1 DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT). The
defence in the data was a hand-written trailing dot on every prefix, which is a convention one editor can
forget; it is now a property of the matcher, drift-tested in both languages, and a trailing dot in the data
is accepted and ignored so it can never become load-bearing again.
⛔ AND THE TEXT A PATTERN SEES IS HYPHEN-NORMALISED, FOR THE SAME REASON. 29 catalog rules spell an operand
name with U+2011 NON-BREAKING HYPHEN where every other rule uses ASCII '-' — SR-13.18.14.3-12 reads
'Identifier‑1 shall be described in the file, working‑storage, …'. An arm written `\bidentifier-1\b`, the
obvious spelling and the one the screen selector's operand arm needs, matches NOTHING there. It cost two
rows (SR-13.18.14.3-12, SR-13.18.35.3-12) on the first measured run of this landing, and it is the worse
failure direction: a selector that silently UNDER-selects leaves the drift test green and the rows
unstamped, so nothing ever contradicts it. Both engines fold U+2010 and U+2011 to '-' before matching.
U+2013 EN DASH is left alone — the standard uses it both as the MINUS-sign glyph and as a clause-range

standard-binary-only.decision: kb/Work PB198 — ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is declined (owner protocol 2026-08-30); docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 2.
$selector: A rule is SOLELY conditioned on standard-binary arithmetic when it names that MODE and names no other
arithmetic mode. Both halves must be about the MODE, not the words:
• 'standard-binary' also names a FLOAT-BINARY USAGE (§11.9.8, §13.18.63) — nothing to do with the
arithmetic mode, so the text arm demands the mode phrase and rejects SR-11.9.8.3-1/-2/-3.
• 'standard decimal floating-point usage' likewise names a USAGE, so the standard-decimal exclusion
carries a negative lookahead — without it AR-15.43.3-3, which IS solely mode-conditioned, was wrongly
excluded.
• A rule reading 'standard-decimal or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect' has content under a mode
we DO support, so it is excluded — which is why the exclusion cannot require a trailing 'arithmetic'
after standard-decimal (GR-14.7.7-3, GR-14.9.26.4-3 slipped through when it did).
⛔ TEXT IS NOT THE ONLY WAY A RULE IS CONDITIONED. Six rules of §8.8.1.4 (the clause TITLED 'Standard-binary
arithmetic') never repeat the phrase — GR-8.8.1.4.2-1 just says 'Any operand of an arithmetic expression
that is not already in SBIDI is converted into SBIDI form' — and a text-only predicate missed every one of
them. The clause arm selects by CLAUSE, which is what the standard actually uses to scope them.
Measured 2026-08-31: 16 rules are solely conditioned on the mode (10 by text, 6 by clause), carrying four
different verdicts before this determination. The mixed rules keep their own — they have reachable content
under a mode we DO support, and stamping them would over-claim. Re-measured unchanged at 16 on 2026-09-02
when the entry was restated in the `arms` shape.
⚖ 17 SINCE kb/Work R43 (2026-09-24), AND THE SEVENTEENTH WAS HELD OUT BY A NOTE. GR-11.9.5.2-2 — 'If the
STANDARD-BINARY phrase is specified, the techniques used in handling arithmetic expressions … shall be as
described for standard-binary arithmetic in 8.8.1.4' — is the mode and nothing else, and it sat outside this
selector only because its NOTE 1 ('Implementors are strongly encouraged to provide support for the
STANDARD-DECIMAL phrase') matched the standard-decimal exclusion (kb/Work PB1517). A NOTE creates no
requirement, so both engines now read NOTE-free text (inventory_schema.NOTE_MARK); measured across every
selector and all 233 catalog rules carrying a NOTE, the cut moved this one row and no other.

$selector: A rule is SOLELY conditioned on the screen facility when NO content survives with the facility absent.
A.4.2 lists 27 elements; the licence for reaching past them to their rules is A.4.1 ¶2's SECOND sentence
(--check OK): 'Any associated syntax rules, general rules, other rules, exception conditions, and I-O
status values are also optional, even if not explicitly listed.'
⚠ AND THAT SENTENCE DOES NOT REACH AN UNLISTED CLAUSE — a correction, because the first draft used it to
license the USING clause (§13.18.61) and LINE format 2 (§13.18.35), neither of which A.4.2 lists. ¶2's
first sentence says the LIST is what identifies optional clauses and formats; the second extends only to
RULES hanging off a listed element. The sound derivation needs no ¶2 at all: A.4.2 item 20 makes the
SCREEN DESCRIPTION ENTRY optional in both its formats, and USING / FROM / TO / LINE-format-2 reach COBOL
only through source-destination-clauses inside that entry, so with the entry absent they have no
syntactic context — which is this selector's own criterion. (Both omissions are defects in the standard,
recorded here because they will be re-found: A.4.2 lists COLUMN clause format 2 as item 7 and has no LINE
item, and lists FROM and TO but not USING.)
A.4.1 NOTE 1 supplies the opposite bound — 'The higher-level constructs or cross-referenced topics are not
optional' — which is why a format-qualified item licenses only that format.
FOUR ARMS, because the standard scopes this module four ways:
• CLAUSE — the 19 clauses A.4.2 names WITHOUT a format qualifier are optional whole (§9.2 Screens,
§13.9 Screen section, §13.17 Screen description entry, and 16 bare-named §13.18 clauses), plus
§13.18.61 USING. Their rules often never say 'screen' (SR-13.18.21.3-1 is just 'The word EOL is
equivalent to the words END OF LINE'), so a text-only predicate misses 52 of them.
• TEXT — rules living in SHARED clauses that name a screen construct: the format-2 half of §13.18.14
COLUMN and §13.18.35 LINE, the screen legs of §13.18.38 OCCURS / §13.18.60 USAGE / §13.18.63 VALUE,
• OPERAND, ×2 — the mechanism the first draft did not have a name for, and the reason five rules were
missing. In §12.3.7 data-name-1 and data-name-2 ARE the CURSOR and CRT STATUS operands: FMT-12.3.7.2
introduces exactly two data-names and they are those. So SR-12.3.7.3-4/-29/-30 are solely conditioned
and carry no screen vocabulary at all. Likewise MINUS and identifier-1 exist ONLY in the screen format
of the COLUMN and LINE clauses — format 1 (report-writer) has PLUS and no identifier operand — which
reaches SR-13.18.14.3-11/-12 and SR-13.18.35.3-11/-12. The LINE pair is the two-arm-dispatch shape
exactly (feedback_two_arm_dispatch): the COLUMN arm was inspected and the LINE arm was not.
⛔ THE TEXT ARM MUST NOT SELECT A GENERAL FORMAT. A diagram is evidence about a CLAUSE, never about one of
its formats, so a multi-format diagram naming 'screen-name-1' in its optional format is NOT solely
conditioned. Without `excludes-kinds`, FMT-14.9.1.2 (ACCEPT formats 1 device + 2 temporal, both supported)
and FMT-14.9.11.2 (DISPLAY format 1 device, supported) — both currently PARTIAL — flip to non-support. The
clause arm still selects FMT-13.17.2 and FMT-13.9.2, whose every format IS screen.
Excluded near-misses share ONE shape: the rule enumerates the screen construct ALONGSIDE its data-division
or report-writer twin, so content survives under a facility we DO support — SR-13.18.20.3-3 (entry-name in
'a data description entry or a report group description entry'), GR-13.18.20.4-1 ('a data, report, or
(GLOBAL). Two more: GR-11.9.10.4-1 lists SCREEN as one of three INITIALIZE targets; SR-12.3.7.3-2
restricts a factory/instance SPECIAL-NAMES to CURSOR and CRT STATUS, so its CONTENT is what it FORBIDS —
every other clause — which survives entirely.
THE ANNEX A.1 ARMS (owner decision R42, 2026-09-24): 'every A.1 item that belongs to a DECLINED module
(screen handling A.4.2, commit/rollback A.4.3 - docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 5 Not claimed) closes as
DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT, the same withdrawal ground as DOC-A.1-84/85/86/173'. The ground is A.1's own
preamble ('When the element is part of a feature that is optional or processor-dependent, the item is not
required if the optional or processor-dependent feature is not implemented', --check OK). Two arms, both
`kinds: [DOC]`: an item whose cross-reference cites one of the clause arm's sections (A.1 items 11, 27,
41, 45, 83, 91, 172, 199), and an item on the SCREEN FORMAT of a shared statement (items 3 and 4 cite
§14.9.1, which ACCEPT's supported device formats share — so the arm also requires the item's own words
'screen format', and items 1, 2, 5 and 111 stay out). The TEXT arm now excludes kind DOC by kind instead
of by the boilerplate pattern 'This item is (required|optional).', which is what held every A.1 row out
before R42. audit_annex_a1.py derives its `unreachable` set from these selectors, so the §7 counter and
the inventory give one answer per item with no edit there.
MEASURED 2026-09-02: 156 of 4,311 rules (110 by clause, 97 by text, 3 by the §12.3.7 operand arm, 6 by the
COLUMN/LINE operand arm; the arms overlap). 149 are blank and 7 already carry DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT, so
the selector FLIPS NOTHING; not one CONFORMS / PARTIAL / DIVERGES / NOT-IMPLEMENTED / NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION
row is touched. See $format-band-residue for the seven rows this shape cannot hold.

commit-and-rollback-only.decision: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 Annex A.4 row 'A.4.3 | Commit and rollback | Not claimed' + §4 item 2, which enumerates the COMMIT and ROLLBACK statements, the APPLY COMMIT clause (§12.4.6.3) and the EC-FLOW-APPLY-COMMIT / EC-FLOW-COMMIT / EC-FLOW-ROLLBACK conditions. $selector: A rule is SOLELY conditioned on the declined module when it lives in one of the module's OWN clauses —
§12.4.6.3 (APPLY COMMIT clause), §14.9.7 (COMMIT), §14.9.36 (ROLLBACK) — or operates over the SET of
active APPLY COMMIT clauses from elsewhere, AND nothing in it survives the module's absence.
⚖ THE RECONCILING PRINCIPLE, because the two bounds below look like a contradiction and a maintainer who
applies the wrong one gets the opposite answer: a rule that CONSTRAINS a supported element is OUT wherever
it sits (A.4.1 makes optional only the rules ASSOCIATED with the optional element); a rule whose entire
CONTENT is module functionality is IN wherever it sits.
⛔ SO THE SCOPE STOPS AT THE MODULE'S OWN CLAUSES. Fourteen rules in CLAIMED or MANDATORY clauses name
APPLY COMMIT only as an antecedent — LOCK MODE (SR-12.4.5.9.3-1), SAME (SR-12.4.6.4.3-11,
(SR-14.9.47.3-2) and fatal-exception handling (GR-14.6.13.1.3-8). Seven of them have no
surviving content — their antecedents are simply unsatisfiable — so 'content survives' is NOT the ground
for those; the ground is that each one's verdict field speaks about CLOSE / OPEN / READ / REWRITE / UNLOCK
/ LOCK MODE / SAME, facilities A.4.7 CLAIMS, and §4.2.7 discharges non-support through user documentation
that declines commit and rollback, never UNLOCK. Stamping them would document a claimed facility as
declined AND — since the drift test PINS every selected row — permanently block their correct adjudication.
⛔ AND THE CLAUSE ARM IS NOT ENOUGH. GR-14.6.11-1 ('An implicit COMMIT statement is executed for the files
specified in all active APPLY COMMIT clauses in the run unit', §14.6.11 Normal run unit termination) is
the module's functionality stated inside a MANDATORY clause. The PLURAL is deliberate: 'active APPLY
COMMIT clauses' marks a rule sweeping the whole SET (the facility itself), while the singular 'a file
subject to an active APPLY COMMIT clause' is the guard form used inside claimed facilities.
THE EXCLUSIONS ARE THE LOAD-BEARING HALF — each drops a rule with SURVIVING content, measured against

$comment: PER-KIND EVIDENCE RULES. `verdicts` says what a VERDICT costs; this says what a ROW OF THIS KIND costs, and
the two are orthogonal. Annex A.1's 222 DOC rows are not behavioural rules: each is an obligation to SPECIFY
and to DOCUMENT an implementor-defined element (ISO 4.2.5 — 'the implementor shall specify, at a minimum, the
implementor-defined language elements that are identified as required. Each implementor-defined language
element specified by the implementor shall be documented if the implementor-defined language element is
identified as requiring user documentation.'). A binder symbol alone cannot discharge that; a DETERMINATION in
docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 can. Before this object existed the schema had no way to say so, and all 222 rows sat
verdict-less while §7 already carried 39 determinations — a third of that work invisible to the burn-down.
⛔ THE ANCHOR IS COMPUTED, NEVER CHOSEN. `anchor-template` expands the row's OWN rule-id, so a DOC row's
register location is a FUNCTION of the row: the next determination's anchor is derived rather than typed, and
a mis-filed one cannot be spelled at all. That is the direct structural answer to kb/Work A11's finding — the
§15.3.3.2 determination filed under item 87 when it belongs to item 202. It is also why §7's item key is the
rule-id `DOC-A.1-<n>` and not the bare number: '#7', an anchor five live rows used, resolves against the digit
7 ANYWHERE in a 790-line document and proves nothing (see `anchored-files` below).
⛔ OBSERVABLE IS DECIDED BY DATA ON THE ROW, NOT BY A HAND LIST. Annex A.1 conditions the documentation duty on
provision ('Documentation required: If the element is provided by the implementor, the implementor's user
documentation shall document the element…'), so 'can a program observe this determination?' IS 'is there
greenfield code that provides it?' — a question whose answer is a PATH, which an independent refuter can
falsify by finding the code, rather than an opinion, which nobody can. `implementation-pattern` reads it off
the row's own code-location list using the SAME greenfield predicate scripts/spec/audit_annex_a1.py's
sweep_source_citations applies to a source path (`p.startswith('Cobol.Net.')` under src/), so the register
audit and the inventory gate cannot disagree — and the legacy CobolSharp engine is evidence of nothing.
⛔ THERE IS NO POLICY ARM, AND ITS ABSENCE IS DELIBERATE. A DOC row closes exactly as every other row does:
its computed anchor is present, it names at least one implementing site under `implementation-pattern`, and a
SPEC-DERIVED test covers it. A row whose ONLY location is the §7 anchor — nothing in the compiler to observe —
therefore stays a GAP. Letting such a row close on the register alone would widen DESIGN-spec-conformance-
review.md §1(a)'s definition of DONE ('a located implementation (a traceability link into src/Cobol.Net.*), OR
a recorded owner documented-non-support decision'), and the owner's completion metric is not an agent's to
redefine. It was also measured to be unreachable: all 39 rows of the first back-fill carry a greenfield site,
so the arm would have had zero instances and its own negative claim ('nothing implements this') would have
been cross-checkable for only 13 of 222 items — a MISSING observation standing in for a NEGATIVE one, which
feedback_verdict_evidence_invariant forbids. The bare question is open as kb/Work PB280 Q2.
⛔ THE ANCHOR IS OBLIGED BY THE ROWS WITH A DETERMINATION TO POINT AT, AND BY NO OTHERS. CONFORMS, PARTIAL
and DIVERGES each assert something about what §7 says, so each owes the §7 row its own rule-id computes.
DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT may assert the opposite — that the CONDITIONING FACILITY is not implemented, so Annex
A.1's own preamble withdraws the item ('When the element is part of a feature that is optional or
processor-dependent, the item is not required if the optional or processor-dependent feature is not
implemented') and there is no determination left to anchor, nor any greenfield site to observe it through.
⛔ BUT THE VERDICT IS NOT THE DISCRIMINATOR — THE REGISTER IS, AND THAT IS A CORRECTION MADE ON 2026-09-02
(kb/Work PB280 Q1). DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT acquired a SECOND ground on a DOC row that day: an item the
standard marks OPTIONAL whose element we do not provide. §7 carries that row — the non-provision IS the
determination — so the row owes its anchor exactly as a CONFORMS row does, and keying the exemption on the
verdict would have excused precisely those rows from naming their own determination, and would have stopped
`check_pins` holding their witness in agreement with §7's `Pinned by` at the moment the witness landed. So
`anchor-exempt-verdicts` names the verdicts that MAY be exempt and the REGISTER decides: exempt when
docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 carries no row for the item, obliged when it does. One predicate per language
(`Schema.anchor_obliged` / `AnchorObliged`) reads it, over one parser per language (`section7_rows` /
`ConformanceRegister`). The audit's own `unreachable_items()` applies the SAME test — a DNS selector's rows
minus the ones §7 documents — so a declined module withdraws its A.1 items from the anchor obligation and
from the REMAINING counter by one act, while a documented decline is counted as the discharged obligation
it is. Keying it on the verdict would have printed '⊘ CANNOT ARISE' about an element this register
documents in full, and dropped REMAINING by two for no work done.
⚠ FOUND BY LANDING THE TWO LANES TOGETHER, 2026-09-02: neither could see it alone. The DOC lane wrote the
anchor rule against a tree where every DOC row was a determination; the derived lane then stamped four DOC
rows (84, 85, 173, 86 — the FORMAT clause and VALIDATE) DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT, and the writer refused the
whole 308-record batch. Adding the anchor to those rows would have been a false claim of a §7 row that does
not and should not exist.
Form: '<repo-relative-path>' or '<repo-relative-path>#<Symbol>'. Several are separated by '; '.
DESIGN CORRECTION against the design doc's original 'file:line'. A line number rots on the next edit to the
file, so 3,790 rows of them would turn the gate permanently red for reasons that have nothing to do with
conformance — and a gate that cries wolf is a gate nobody reads. A SYMBOL survives refactoring, moves with
the code it names, and fails only when the thing it points at actually stops existing, which is precisely
the event worth failing on.
The symbol class admits '-' because a register anchor is not a C# identifier: `docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-2`
is the computed anchor of the A.1 item-2 row (see `kinds`), and before this one character the whole 39-record
back-fill failed shape validation on that line alone.
$anchored-files-comment: A file whose fragments are a NAMED ANCHOR SPACE rather than a code symbol. The gate resolves '#Symbol' by a
word search over the file body: exact for a C# identifier, worthless for a number. Five live rows carried
`docs/CONFORMANCE.md#7` and were state OK on that basis — '#7' matches the digit 7 anywhere in a 790-line
document — and three more cited the BARE path, which resolves on File.Exists alone and is weaker still. So:
every fragment on a listed file must match its pattern, AND a listed file may not be cited without one.
The pattern is an ALTERNATION over the anchor spaces docs/CONFORMANCE.md ACTUALLY has, derived from the
document's own section keys rather than from one section's needs: §7's Annex A.1 rows are keyed by the
inventory rule-id `DOC-A.1-<n>`; §1 is the §4.2.16 conformance summary, which RV-15.31.3-2 legitimately
anchors as '4.2.16'; §5's Annex A.4 rows are keyed 'A.4.<n>'. ⚠ §2's Annex A.3 rows are keyed by a BARE
NUMBER and therefore have NO anchor space — anchoring one would reproduce the '#7' defect exactly, and the
answer when a row needs it is to re-key §2 the way §7 was re-keyed, not to widen this pattern. §3 and §4 are
prose lists with no keys at all.

$comment: The covering spec-derived test. Every form RESOLVES to something on disk, so 'tested' can never be a claim
the inventory merely makes about itself — which is the difference between a burn-down and a self-report.
Several refs are separated by '; '.
Each form is machine-readable so the gate does not carry a second copy of this table: 'path-template' is
the repo-relative path the ref's body fills in at {0}, and 'test-dir' marks the xUnit forms, whose body is
<Class>.<Method> and which resolve to a [Fact]/[Theory] method of that name in <Class>.cs under that
directory. Adding a form is an edit to THIS object and nothing else.
⛔ RESOLVING ON DISK IS NOT ENOUGH — IT MUST BE SPEC-DERIVED. DESIGN-spec-conformance-review.md §1(c)
requires a covering test 'whose expected value is COMPUTED FROM THE SPEC, never copied from an
implementation oracle', and CLAUDE.md rule 1 names the NIST goldens, the legacy engine and the GnuCOBOL
differential as regression NETS WITH KNOWN HOLES, never authority. A differential is structurally blind to
a violation both implementations share — and many of this compiler's defects were ported FROM the legacy,
so agreeing with it is evidence of nothing. A row closed on that basis is a burn-down moving on the exact
evidence the standard forbids.
So each form carries 'spec-derived', and a resolving verdict needs at least ONE ref that has it. A
non-spec-derived ref is still worth RECORDING — knowing NIST also exercises a rule is useful — it just
cannot be what closes the row. This was found the hard way: the first Phase-B batch came back with 19
CONFORMS rows, and 7 of them rested on nothing but a NIST golden or a *_MatchesLegacy differential.
$disqualifying-comment: An xUnit form CAN be spec-derived, so the form alone cannot decide it — but this repo names the two kinds
apart by convention (*_PinnedToSpec versus *_MatchesLegacy), and a method whose own name says it matches
the legacy is self-evidently not computed from the spec. Any test-ref whose method name matches one of
these is treated as NOT spec-derived, whatever its form says.

nist.why-not: A NIST CCVS golden is a REGRESSION NET, not an oracle (CLAUDE.md rule 1). Record it as corroboration; it can never be what closes a row.

characterization.why-not: A characterization snapshot pins CURRENT behaviour byte-for-byte — it is the definition of a differential, and it would happily pin a defect.

$comment: ⛔ THE ONE ALTERNATIVE TO A SPEC-DERIVED TEST, AND THE OWNER OPENED IT — kb/Work PB386, 2026-09-03.
DESIGN-spec-conformance-review.md §1.1 is the definition; this is that definition as DATA.
Some normative rules impose no obligation a conforming program can observe. The standard may declare the
result UNDEFINED — §4.4 2): 'Situations in which the results of executing a statement are explicitly
undefined or unpredictable are identified in A.2, Undefined language element list. A COBOL run unit that
allows these situations to happen is a conforming run unit' — or the rule's antecedent may be false for
every state this implementation can reach, or its consequent may be indistinguishable from another rule's.
For such a row §1(c) is not unmet but UNMEETABLE: a golden written for it would pin an IMPLEMENTATION

$refusals: The bounds the owner set, encoded rather than described (record_verdicts.validate reports each by name):
1) a derivation on a row that ALREADY carries a spec-derived test-ref — that row demonstrably has an
observable obligation, so the premise is false for it;
2) a derivation on a row whose verdict does not RESOLVE;
3) a derivation on a row of a kind that obliges a register determination docs/CONFORMANCE.md does not
carry — the documentation obligation is not yet STATED, so there is nothing to derive about;
4) an `undefined-A.2` arm naming an item that does not resolve to this row;
5) a missing or wrong owner signature;
6) a `derivation` value that is not the COMPUTED anchor, or one docs/CONFORMANCE.md §8 has no row for.

undefined-A.2.meaning: The standard's own Annex A.2 lists this rule as explicitly undefined, so every behaviour conforms and no expected value exists to derive. MECHANICAL: A.2 item <n> must resolve to this row's rule-id in `undefined-list`.

unpopulatable-antecedent.meaning: The rule's antecedent is false for every state this implementation can reach. A REVIEWED ARGUMENT: the Names cell must STATE the closed set that makes it unreachable — a dash, an 'n/a' or a bare word is refused, because an argument nobody can check is the free-text escape hatch this mechanism exists not to be.

indistinguishable-consequent.meaning: The rule's consequent is byte-identical to another rule's for every argument the two admit, so no conforming program can distinguish them. A REVIEWED ARGUMENT: the Names cell must be a rule-id that EXISTS in the catalog and is not this row's own.

definitional.meaning: kb/Work R43 item 4 (owner, 2026-09-24, extending PB386; answers PB468 Q9): the rule DEFINES a property of the USER's program (a conforming run unit, §4.4) and imposes no obligation on the implementation, so no program can observe it apart from the rules that DO oblige the implementation. A REVIEWED ARGUMENT: the Names cell must open 'defines' and state the property and whose it is; a rule whose subject is the implementation or the implementor is never this arm.
